strings.name: Shohei Ohtani
strings.summary: Shohei Ohtani has combined pitching and hitting in Japanese professional baseball and MLB, changing ideas about player specialization in modern baseball. From Hanamaki Higashi High School he joined the Fighters, then played in the United States for the Angels and Dodgers. He won league MVP awards and helped Japan win the 2023 World Baseball Classic. In 2024 he became MLB’s first player with at least 50 home runs and 50 stolen bases in one season.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verified milestones through 2026-11-12; sources checked on 13 November 2026. This is not an event-by-event or live record.
strings.influence.rationale: His breakthroughs as a two-way pitcher and hitter, together with Most Valuable Player achievements, have reshaped perceptions of roles in modern baseball.

strings.highlights.two-way.title: Two-way achievement
strings.highlights.two-way.text: His pitching and hitting contributions earned him the unanimous 2021 American League MVP award.
strings.highlights.fifty-fifty.title: First 50–50 season
strings.highlights.fifty-fifty.text: On 19 September 2024 he became the first MLB player to reach 50 home runs and 50 stolen bases in a season.
strings.timeline.mvp26.title: Second in NL MVP voting
strings.timeline.mvp26.text: He finished second in the 2026 National League MVP vote after injuries affected the end of his season.
strings.timeline.mvp25.title: Fourth MVP award
strings.timeline.mvp25.text: He won the 2025 National League MVP, his fourth MLB MVP and third in consecutive years.
strings.timeline.record24.title: Reached 50–50
strings.timeline.record24.text: Three home runs and two steals against Miami made him MLB’s first player with a 50–50 season.
strings.timeline.classic23.title: Helped Japan win the Classic
strings.timeline.classic23.text: He struck out Mike Trout for the final out of the World Baseball Classic final, helping Japan defeat the United States.
strings.timeline.mvp21.title: First MLB MVP
strings.timeline.mvp21.text: His pitching and hitting for the Angels earned a unanimous American League MVP, establishing his two-way path.
strings.timeline.rookie18.title: MLB Rookie of the Year
strings.timeline.rookie18.text: He joined the Los Angeles Angels in the United States and won American League Rookie of the Year in his first MLB season.
strings.timeline.japan16.title: Japan Series success
strings.timeline.japan16.text: His pitching and hitting helped the Fighters win the Japan Series, and he received the Pacific League MVP.
strings.timeline.debut13.title: Japanese professional debut
strings.timeline.debut13.text: After being selected in the first round in 2012, he began playing Japanese professional baseball for the Hokkaido Nippon-Ham Fighters.
strings.timeline.school10.title: Training at Hanamaki Higashi
strings.timeline.school10.text: He continued his baseball training at Hanamaki Higashi High School in Iwate, preparing for professional competition.
